prompt: Set the system volume to 65 percent. Then undo that change.
why: THE FEATURE'S ABSENCE COST THIS USER SOMETHING REAL: a session set the system volume to 42% and could not put it back, because nothing had recorded the previous value. This row is that defect, turned into a check. Setup puts the volume at a known 30% so the target is not whatever the machine happened to be at, and the verify reads the level straight out of the Windows audio endpoint with PowerShell — a different route from the one the agent used, so a reversal the agent merely believes in does not pass. It would FAIL if `undo` restored nothing, restored the wrong level, or reported success without the endpoint agreeing. It deliberately does NOT assert what the agent said: the sentence is not the evidence, the endpoint is. Manual, because it changes something the user can hear.
